name: Society of Jesus (Jesuits)
note: Religious order founded 1540 by Ignatius of Loyola; spearhead of Counter-Reformation education and overseas mission.

name: Discalced Carmelites
note: Reformed contemplative Carmelite branch founded by Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross (1560s–70s).

name: North American Martyrs
note: Eight Jesuit missionaries martyred in New France/Iroquoia 1642–1649; canonized 1930.

name: Ignatius of Loyola
note: Basque founder of the Society of Jesus (1540); author of the Spiritual Exercises; patron of retreats and spiritual directors.

name: Francis Xavier
note: Jesuit co-founder; pioneering missionary to India, the Malay archipelago and Japan; patron of the missions.

name: Teresa of Ávila
note: Spanish Carmelite mystic and reformer; Doctor of the Church; author of The Interior Castle and her Life.

name: John of the Cross
note: Spanish Carmelite mystic, poet and reformer with Teresa of Ávila; Doctor of the Church; author of The Dark Night of the Soul.

name: Philip Neri
note: "Apostle of Rome"; founder of the Congregation of the Oratory; figure of Catholic renewal and joyful piety.

name: Charles Borromeo
note: Cardinal-archbishop of Milan; leading implementer of the Council of Trent's reforms and seminary system.

name: Peter Canisius
note: Dutch Jesuit, Doctor of the Church; catechist who led the Catholic recovery in German-speaking lands.

name: Robert Bellarmine
note: Italian Jesuit cardinal, theologian and controversialist; Doctor of the Church; patron of catechists and canonists.

name: Aloysius Gonzaga
note: Italian Jesuit novice who died nursing plague victims in Rome (1591); patron of youth and of those with epidemics.

name: Rose of Lima
note: Peruvian Dominican tertiary mystic; first canonized saint of the Americas; patroness of Latin America.

name: Martín de Porres
note: Afro-Peruvian Dominican lay brother of Lima; healer and almsgiver; patron of social justice and of mixed-race peoples.

name: Turibius of Mogrovejo
note: Archbishop of Lima; reforming Tridentine pastor of colonial Peru; patron of the Latin American episcopate.

name: Vincent de Paul
note: French founder of the Congregation of the Mission (Vincentians) and co-founder of the Daughters of Charity; patron of charitable works.

name: Louise de Marillac
note: French co-founder with Vincent de Paul of the Daughters of Charity; patroness of social workers.

name: Francis de Sales
note: Bishop of Geneva, Doctor of the Church; author of Introduction to the Devout Life; co-founder of the Visitation order.

name: Jane Frances de Chantal
note: French widow and co-founder with Francis de Sales of the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary.

name: Camillus de Lellis
note: Italian founder of the Camillians (Ministers of the Sick); patron of the sick, nurses and hospitals.

name: John of God
note: Portuguese founder of the Brothers Hospitallers; patron of hospitals, the sick and nurses.

name: Catherine dei Ricci
note: Italian Dominican mystic of Prato known for ecstasies of the Passion; correspondent of reformers.

name: Peter Claver
note: Spanish Jesuit "slave of the slaves" who ministered to the enslaved at Cartagena; patron of African missions and human rights.

name: Alphonsus Liguori
note: Italian founder of the Redemptorists, Doctor of the Church and moral theologian; patron of confessors and moralists.

name: Paul of the Cross
note: Italian founder of the Passionists, devoted to the Passion of Christ; baroque-era mystic and preacher.

name: Benedict Joseph Labre
note: French mendicant pilgrim and "beggar of Rome" (d. 1783); patron of the homeless and of pilgrims.

name: Isaac Jogues
note: French Jesuit missionary martyred by the Mohawk in 1646; chief among the North American Martyrs.

name: Jean de Brébeuf
note: French Jesuit missionary to the Huron, martyred 1649; among the North American Martyrs; patron of Canada.

name: Peter Faber
note: Savoyard priest, one of the first companions and co-founders of the Society of Jesus; noted director of the Spiritual Exercises.

name: Francis Borgia
note: Spanish duke turned Jesuit; third Superior General of the Society of Jesus and major early Jesuit organizer.

name: Stanislaus Kostka
note: Polish Jesuit novice (d. 1568); patron of novices and of Catholic youth.

name: Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi
note: Florentine Carmelite mystic of the Counter-Reformation, known for ecstasies and visions.

name: Joseph of Cupertino
note: Italian Conventual Franciscan mystic famed for reported levitations; patron of students and air travelers.

name: Josaphat Kuntsevych
note: Ruthenian Greek-Catholic archbishop of Polotsk, martyred 1623 for the Union of Brest; first Eastern-rite saint formally canonized.

name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
note: Marian apparition to Juan Diego at Tepeyac, Mexico (1531); the tilma image; patroness of the Americas and a Marian title of the Virgin Mary.
